Vitals: temp_c=39.1, hr_bpm=142, rr_bpm=39
Microscopy: not performed
Culture & sensitivity: not available

Diagnosis: Canine Parvovirus

Differentials considered: Haemorrhagic gastroenteritis, Coccidiosis, Intestinal foreign body, Bacterial enteritis

Treatment:
  - Drug: Supportive care (no specific antiviral)
  - Dose: None mg/kg
  - Route: IV
  - Frequency: N/A
  - Duration: 0 day(s)

Supportive care:
  - aggressive IV fluid and electrolyte therapy
  - antiemetics (maropitant / metoclopramide)
  - broad-spectrum antibiotics for secondary bacterial translocation / sepsis
  - nutritional support and strict isolation / biosecurity

Withdrawal period: 0 days (milk/meat must not enter the food chain before this elapses).
Follow-up: review in 5 days.

Rationale: This dog (Labrador Retriever, 7 months) was evaluated for profuse haemorrhagic diarrhoea, vomiting, lethargy, dehydration and pyrexia or hypothermia. No microscopy parasite was identified; the assessment rests on clinical signs and history. No culture & sensitivity report was available for this case. Because canine parvovirus is a viral enteritis: there is NO antiviral cure; survival depends on intensive supportive care, Canine Parvovirus is the most likely diagnosis over Haemorrhagic gastroenteritis, Coccidiosis, Intestinal foreign body and Bacterial enteritis. Recommended: supportive care (no specific antiviral) with supportive nursing. Fever measured 39.1 C.

Microscopy: not performed
Culture & sensitivity: not available

Diagnosis: Contagious Caprine Pleuropneumonia

Differentials considered: Peste des Petits Ruminants, Pasteurellosis, Verminous pneumonia, Caseous lymphadenitis

Treatment:
  - Drug: Tylosin
  - Dose: 10.0 mg/kg
  - Route: IM
  - Frequency: q24h
  - Duration: 3 day(s)
  - Total dose for this 45.1 kg animal: 451.0 mg

Supportive care:
  - NSAID for pyrexia and pleuritic pain
  - long-acting oxytetracycline is an accepted alternative

Rationale: Presenting complaint in this Toggenburg cross goat (71 months) was pyrexia, painful cough, nasal discharge and lethargy. Recorded fever of 41.7 C. No microscopy parasite was identified; the assessment rests on clinical signs and history. Given that CCPP is caused by Mycoplasma capricolum subsp. capripneumoniae and responds to macrolide/tetracycline antibiotics, a working diagnosis of Contagious Caprine Pleuropneumonia was reached, with Peste des Petits Ruminants, Pasteurellosis, Verminous pneumonia and Caseous lymphadenitis on the differential list. No culture & sensitivity report was available for this case. Treatment: Tylosin 10.0 mg/kg IM plus adjunctive supportive care.
